observation_kind: targeted current official INSPIRE release, catalogue/search, LIDAR multi-resolution and Terrain 50 capture-integrity checks; not independent bulk HTTP fetches
rules: The current indexed download page states that the INSPIRE dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
New INSPIRE Index Polygon files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
INSPIRE polygons are downloadable by local-authority area.
A geographic information system is required to view the downloaded GML polygon files.
The dataset shows locations and indicative extents of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open dataset developed to comply with the INSPIRE Directive.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary appears in both local-authority files.
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID that relates to a registered title.
The exact land extent in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons and requires the individual title plan.
One title number may contain several separate polygons, each with its own INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can indicate unregistered land, leasehold registration or another tenure excluded from the dataset.
Reuse requires HM Land Registry attribution and an additional Ordnance Survey attribution when polygon geometry is reused.
Planning datasets are grouped into Geography, Category, Legal Instrument, Document, Organisation, Policy, Metric and Timetable types.
The current dataset catalogue lists 56 Geography datasets.
Title boundary is listed in the Geography dataset group.
The public entity search exposes a typology filter.
The public entity search exposes dataset, organisation and postcode-or-UPRN filters.
The public entity search provides a JSON download option for result sets.
The 2m composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England at two-metre spatial resolution.
The 2m DTM is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
Surface objects are removed with bespoke algorithms and manual editing to form a terrain-only model.
The 2022 2m composite combines Time Stamped archive surveys and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
For repeated surveys, the newest best-resolution source is selected.
Bilinear interpolation is used where source data is resampled before merging.
The 2022 composite source period runs from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
The 2m data is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters in five-kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Individual source surveys are documented with vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The metadata records no public-access constraints and use under the Open Government Licence.
The 10m composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England at ten-metre spatial resolution.
The 10m DTM is resampled from the 2m composite using bilinear interpolation.
The 10m product is supplied as a single GeoTIFF raster aligned to the OS National Grid.
The official record lists no data services or area-of-interest resources for the 10m product.
The full 10m download is supplied as LIDAR_Composite_10m_DTM_2022.zip.
The official 10m metadata identifier is ce8fe7e7-bed0-4889-8825-19b042e128d2.
The source TIN model is not widely supported by GIS software, so grid and contour products are interpolated from it.
OS Terrain 50 uses a more generalised feature representation because it is designed for small-scale products.
Underground features are not recorded because they are not the ground surface.
Overhead features are removed from the terrain data.
The DTM is intended to be free of spikes and wells that do not represent real terrain.
Road carriageways and railway track beds are modelled as smooth surfaces.
Most data should present without visible tile edges or discernible height differences.
Small edges or differences can remain between newly captured and older content.
Small tile edges can occur in tidal areas because local tidal levels differ.
Supported structures such as bridges, viaducts, cranes, elevated buildings and piers are modelled.
Associated slopes and embankments along supported routes are also modelled.
Outside supported-structure cases, the surface is modelled smooth and flat, though not necessarily horizontal.
The outer limits, shape and depth of mineral workings and landfill sites are captured.
Temporary spoil heaps that do not represent terrain at capture time are removed.
Contained flat-water bodies greater than 0.7 hectares have their limits captured.
The recorded water height is the lowest height of the surrounding terrain data.
Captured contained-water surfaces are modelled as flat.
The official known-data-issues page currently lists no live known issues for OS Terrain 50.
Official XML schema resources are provided for contour products, gridded products and viewing-style metadata.
